summary: Mobile Task CRUD + multi-assignee end-to-end tested on Expo web preview (390x1000) as serkan/19071987. 6 of 7 requested flows PASS; 1 flow (DELETE via task-form-delete-button) is BLOCKED by react-native-web's no-op Alert.alert — the confirm dialog never renders on web and the destructive callback never runs, so no DELETE /api/tasks/{id} request is issued. PASSING FLOWS: (1) task-create-fab opens task-form-modal; (2) validation — saving with empty title keeps modal open and shows 'Görev başlığı gerekli'; (3) CREATE personal task with title/description + due chip 'Bugün' + category chip 'Fason Verme' → modal closes, new row 'TESTQA98537 Personal' appears under Fason Verme with due 04.08.2026; (4) tapping row BODY (right side, not checkbox) opens edit modal PRE-FILLED with title + description + due (04.08.2026 chip active) + Fason Verme category chip active; (5) editing title to '... EDITED' + KAYDET closes modal and updates the row in the list; (6) MULTI-ASSIGNEE on create — assignee-search-input with 'ahmet' returns task-form-assignee-result-<id>, tapping it adds task-form-assignee-chip-<id>, Oluştur closes modal with no error (task is assigned only to ahmet so not in serkan's scope=mine list — expected); (7) checkbox toggle regression — tapping task-toggle-<id> flips the status pill and PATCH /api/tasks/{id} fires (verified via change in row inner text). FAILING FLOW: (5-bis) DELETE — clicking task-form-delete-button on the web preview issues NO network request, no window.confirm/window.alert fires, no in-page overlay appears; body remains at the tasks list with the task still visible. Verified by network interception (`page.on('request')` captured 0 entries for /api/tasks after the click). RCA: /app/mobile/src/components/TaskFormModal.tsx:150-168 uses `Alert.alert('Görevi sil', ..., [{text:'Vazgeç'},{text:'Sil', onPress: async () => api.deleteTask(...)}])`. On native iOS/Android this would render a proper action sheet, but react-native-web's Alert shim is non-interactive (no button rendering, no promise), so the 'Sil' onPress handler never fires on the Expo web preview. This is both a testability gap (delete can't be verified via the Expo web preview that reviewers use) and a real user-facing bug for anyone using the app via the web preview. Native (real iOS/Android build) should still work. NO REGRESSIONS observed vs iteration_105: login → tasks list of 17 (grew to 19 during test as expected) → toggle → profile logout all still functional. Only remaining console warning is the known 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' one from RN Web / Expo Router internals (non-blocking, unchanged).

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping task-form-delete-button on Expo web preview does nothing — react-native-web's Alert.alert renders no buttons, so the destructive `Sil` onPress never fires and DELETE /api/tasks/{id} is never issued. Task remains in the list. Native mobile likely works; web preview is broken and delete is untestable via web.

integration_issues.issue: No DELETE /api/tasks/{id} request fired after tapping delete on web preview (confirmed via request interception).

react_native_issues.issue: Used for the delete confirmation in TaskFormModal but is a no-op on react-native-web (Expo web preview). Recommend replacing with a custom cross-platform confirm — e.g. an inline <Modal transparent> with 'Vazgeç' and 'Sil' pressables — so the flow works and is testable on all surfaces. Reference: /app/mobile/src/components/TaskFormModal.tsx:150-168

Console warning 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' still emits once during login (unchanged from iteration_105). Non-blocking, origin appears to be RN Web / Expo Router internals — no user-code offender found. Reference: n/a (framework-level).

action_items: Replace `Alert.alert(...)` in /app/mobile/src/components/TaskFormModal.tsx:150-168 with a cross-platform in-app confirm modal (e.g. a small <Modal transparent> or a reusable ConfirmDialog component) so delete works on the Expo web preview and remains testable end-to-end. Native Alert.alert renders on iOS/Android but is a silent no-op on react-native-web.

(Optional) Consider adding a `testID` on the confirm dialog's 'Sil' / 'Vazgeç' buttons (e.g. task-form-delete-confirm / task-form-delete-cancel) once the custom modal is in place, so future e2e can assert on it directly.

TaskFormModal.tsx: on edit save (isEdit branch) `category_id: categoryId ?? ''` sends an empty string to unset the category. Verify backend PATCH accepts '' as 'clear category' rather than treating it as a validation error — worked in this test because we kept the category, but worth confirming.
TaskFormModal.tsx:150-168 — Alert.alert for destructive confirmation is not cross-platform on RN Web. See action item.
tasks.tsx:249 `onPressTask={openEdit}` correctly wires row-body taps to the edit modal (verified). onToggleTask stays wired to the checkbox press only — no accidental double-fire.

TaskFormModal.tsx: on create, the creator's own id is NOT auto-added to assignee_user_ids — a task created with only 'ahmet' as an assignee is invisible in serkan's `scope=mine` list. Modal-closes-without-error is the only success signal on the create-for-someone-else path. This matches the review request's guidance but is subtle UX; consider a toast confirmation for clarity.

rca of the issue: DELETE flow (react-native Alert.alert on Expo web preview): react-native-web ships a stub Alert.alert that either calls window.alert(title+message) with no buttons OR is a complete no-op depending on version. In this project the stub is silent — clicking `Görevi Sil` runs Alert.alert(...) which returns immediately; the destructive button's onPress callback (which contains api.deleteTask) is never scheduled. Verified by intercepting page.on('request') across the click and observing zero /api/tasks/* traffic; also confirmed by absence of any dialog event and absence of any Vazgeç/Sil DOM overlay. Mitigation: replace Alert.alert with a custom <Modal transparent> in TaskFormModal.tsx (or a reusable ConfirmDialog) that renders real Pressables for Vazgeç/Sil and wires the destructive onPress to api.deleteTask — this works on both native (iOS/Android) and web preview and is straightforward to add testIDs to.
